content.text: I sin bok "Notes and Recollections" skrev Mises: "The Nazis looted my library and collections. The manuscripts I had worked on during my years in Vienna were lost. I was deeply affected by these losses. However, I managed to escape and start anew. The Nazis chased me out of my home country and off the continent."

Denne uttalelsen er fra Mises selv, hentet fra hans personlige memoarer om opplevelsen med Nazi-forfølgelse.

### 2. Konkrete begivenheter under Anschluss (mars 1938)

citations.cited_text: On the day German forces entered Vienna during the Anschluss, they raided his apartment, confiscating his papers and library.
citations.title: Ludwig von Mises - Wikipedia

content.text: På dagen tyske styrker gjorde sitt inntog i Wien under Anschluss, ransomlet de hans leilighet, konfiskerte hans papirer og bibliotek.

### 3. Mises' advarsel fra 1927 – profetiske ord

content.text: I 1927 sa Mises til sin tidligere student Fritz Machlup fra sitt kontor ved Vienna Chamber of Commerce: "Maybe grass will grow there, because our civilization will end." Han foreslå at de kanskje måtte emigrere til Argentina. "Friedrich A. Hayek could be employed as the headwaiter, Mises said, while Machlup, no doubt, would be the nightclub's resident gigolo... He would have to look for work as the doorman, for what else, Mises asked, would he be qualified to do?"

Dette sitatet viser at Mises allerede i 1927 fryktet kollaps av europeisk sivilisasjon.

---

### 4. Mises' flukt til Sveits i 1934

citations.cited_text: In 1934, Mises fled from Austria to Switzerland to escape the Nazis, and in 1940 he emigrated from Switzerland to the United States.

Rappard, medgrunnlegger og direktør for Graduate Institute of International Studies i Genève, Mises en stilling som professor i internasjonale økonomiske forhold. Mises tok denne posisjonen høsten 1934, men hans stilling ble fornyet årlig og han forble i Genève til juli 1940, da han og hans kone Margit emigrerte til USA i skyggen av tysk okkupasjon av nabolandet Frankrike.

### 5. Mises' ville ikke forlate Genève – hans kones innisten

I begged him, I implored him to leave, to think of me, if he would not think of himself."

Among his persecutors and tormentors most assuredly would have been some of his own colleagues at the Vienna Chamber of Commerce."
